STEP 1 - Scene: A small light snack or side: a few broccoli florets and one whole clementine/mandarin-type orange on a white plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel: White square-ish plate, roughly 22 cm across (side-plate size). Area ≈ 3.14 x (11)^2 ≈ 380 cm^2 (treating it as roughly round; square-ish area is similar).

STEP 3 - Items:
- Broccoli florets (about 4 pieces, cluster of small florets)
- Whole citrus fruit (clementine/mandarin, about 6 cm diameter)

STEP 4 - Area:
- Broccoli: covers about 6% of vessel area (~23 cm^2)
- Citrus fruit: about 7% (~27 cm^2 footprint, roughly 6 cm diameter circle)
- Total food coverage ≈ 13% of the plate, consistent with a small amount.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Broccoli: 23 cm^2 x 3 cm ≈ 70 ml (outer envelope of the florets)
- Citrus: a whole fruit of ~6 cm diameter ≈ 113 ml volume (sphere), roughly 27 cm^2 footprint x 4.5 cm height ≈ 120 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Broccoli: 70 ml x 0.5 g/ml ≈ 35 g (florets are loose, bulk density at the low end of cut vegetables)
- Citrus: the whole fruit is dense, ~0.9 g/ml; a clementine of this size weighs about 100 g. Use 100 g.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Broccoli: 35 g x 34 kcal/100 g ≈ 12 kcal
- Citrus (mandarin/clementine): 100 g x 47 kcal/100 g ≈ 47 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Four small broccoli florets plus one clementine is a plausible small snack. Total ≈ 135 g and ≈ 59 kcal, which fits what is visible and is well below a full plate.

Total: about 135 g, about 59 kcal.
